check.reason: The target is the system: Medicare, the AI prior-authorization experiment, and the opaque, denial-prone bureaucracy. It doesn't mock patients, reporters or private individuals. It uses no invented numbers or quotes and doesn't touch death, children or violence. The take is dry and deadpan, with a real satirical turn in the closing line about automating the appeals process. It also reflects the real story, which is about new documents raising questions about the experiment. The one soft spot is that 'handed prior authorization to an algorithm' slightly overstates what is a limited pilot. It reads as satirical exaggeration rather than a factual misstatement, so it passes.

pick.title: New documents raise more questions about Medicare’s AI prior-authorization experiment
pick.headline: Medicare's AI Prior-Authorization Experiment Raises More Questions, Answers Still Pending Review
pick.take: Medicare has handed prior authorization to an algorithm, and new documents suggest nobody is entirely sure how it works. That's consistent with the human version, which also runs on opaque criteria and ends in a denial. The efficiency gains will arrive once the appeals process is automated too.
